notes.5: Question 5 was answered correctly by 16 per cent of the candidates who chose option A . 26 per cent chose option B , 22 per cent chose option C and 36 per cent chose option D . The question required candidates to understand what was meant by, and identify and example of, market failure. In economics, market failure is a situation in which the allocation of goods and services is not efficient. That is, there exists another conceivable outcome where at least one individual may be made better-off without making someone else worse-off. Option A fulfils that definition.

A pension and a paid holiday (option B ) would occur when the employee was not working and thus would not be a wage for a task undertaken.

Someone wishing regular hours would not find farming suitable as the hours are long and irregular.
